name: Joshua Rotenberg
body: At Solenzo, I own onboarding end to end for every client, from the signed agreement through their first working deliverable. I sequence Google Business Profile setup first, before any automation, because it is the one piece of work a client can verify himself, a live, complete listing, without needing me to explain anything. That sequencing is the standard opening move for every engagement today, not a one-off choice.

At Wix, I built the onboarding process for a brand-new vertical from a blank page. It was still proof of concept, so I started by defining the CRM fields the team needed for onboarding and outbound sales, standardizing data capture before we scaled headcount, then used that structure to build new-hire training and sales training for tenured account executives. The vertical went from proof of concept to a profitable line, run consistently instead of ad hoc.

At Birdeye, regular utilization reviews across the 15 to 20 reseller partners I managed, not a complaint, caught it: several partners had been onboarded and trained, but adoption had quietly stalled after launch. I went back to them directly, found where the process had broken down, and rebuilt the training and communication cadence that had let them go quiet. That habit is a real part of why I retained all but one partner (about 94%) over my tenure.

At Accelo, I built the sequenced implementation plan for an incoming client before the deal closed, ranking which systems needed to change and in what order. That ranked plan became the handoff I gave the implementation team, so they inherited a decision already made about where the risk sat instead of re-interviewing the client from scratch. Implementation started executing on day one instead of losing a week to rediscovery.
I'd welcome a conversation about how these fit EULER's onboarding function. I'm available at 303-726-5037 or jrotnbrg@gmail.com.
